newsitem.title: USA: Midwest business optimism tempering - BankAmerica.
newsitem.headline: Midwest business optimism tempering - BankAmerica.

text.p: Midwest business executives are less optimistic about the economy for 1997 than they were six months ago, but are not actually pessimistic, according to BankAmerica Corp's Bank of America Illinois unit.
The bank's Midwest Business Confidence index fell to 44.2 at the end of 1996 from 47.4 mid-year, the bank said.

"These executives are far from pessimistic about business prospects in the first half of 1997," said Marcus Acheson IV, head of commercial banking for Bank of America Illinois. "Their confidence level is tempered because they question whether the national economy can continue to grow next year as fast as this year and whether the booming stock market can 'boom' eternally."

Of those surveyed, 72 percent believe labor costs will increase in the next six months, while three percent think they will decrease, Bank of America said. That compares with 56 percent who predicted increases and six percent who forecast decreases six months ago.
Twenty-seven percent expect to increase staff, seven percent expect to reduce staff and 65 percent expect staffing to remain the same, the survey of 579 middle-market companies said.
Meanwhile, 77 percent expect sales to increase, compared to 69 percent six months ago.
